To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the relationship between symptom reporting and job performance is not a simple one; 2) the effects of symptom reporting on job performance are mediated by the effects of symptom severity; and 3) the effects of invalid symptom reporting are moderated by the extent to which the job performance measure captures the core aspects of the job.
(a) symptom reporting is a complex, multidimensional phenomenon and (b) the use of symptom reporting as an indicator of employee well-being is not straightforward.

the role of symptom reporting in the prediction of future performance.
the development and validation of a new approach to assessing the validity of self-reports of symptoms.
the role of symptom reporting in the prediction of health care use and health care costs.
